section_summary: This section documents the field execution, local problems, and Allied diplomatic policymaking concerning agricultural reforms in occupied Japan during 1948 and 1949. It features extensive survey and inspection reports by W. I. Ladejinsky and Jay Dixon Edwards detailing land reform progress, the dissolution of the wartime Nogyokai, and severe tax, credit, and grain quota grievances among farmers in northern Honshu. The remaining documents trace Far Eastern Commission deliberations and interdepartmental U.S. directives (Directives Serial No. 97 and 103) establishing occupation policies for democratic farmers' cooperatives, unions, and agrarian land redistribution.

subfiles.about: Evaluates the performance of military government teams in supervising Japanese authorities and emphasizes the central role of land reform in occupation policy.
subfiles.from: W. I. Ladejinsky (Department of the Army Consultant)
subfiles.summary: Ladejinsky commends military government teams for advancing SCAP land reform while maintaining positive relations with Japanese officials, but warns that severe personnel shortages and high turnover threaten the occupation's transition toward civilian governance and institutional education.
subfiles.title: Report on Land Reform and Military Government Teams in Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum by Jay Dixon Edwards reporting on an agricultural orientation survey trip to four northern Honshu prefectures.
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald (United States Political Adviser for Japan)
subfiles.summary: Transmits a memorandum by Jay Dixon Edwards reporting on an orientation survey trip through northern Honshu examining land reform progress, agricultural cooperatives, rice quotas, and tax grievances.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 624: Agricultural Survey Trip to Northern Japan

subfiles.about: Details the findings of a ten-day survey trip to Niigata, Akita, Aomori, and Yamagata prefectures investigating land reform, cooperatives, crop quotas, and agricultural taxation.
subfiles.summary: Edwards reports on an extensive survey trip through Niigata, Akita, Aomori, and Yamagata prefectures to investigate agricultural conditions alongside SCAP economist Robert S. Hardie. While arable land acquisition and transfer to tenant farmers were substantially advanced, the disposal of reclaimable public and private land lagged severely across all four prefectures. The dissolution of the wartime Nogyokai and organization of new democratic cooperatives encountered friction regarding asset division and whether to form unified or specialized federations. In addition, farmers faced acute financial distress and rapidly depleted bank deposits due to heavy, arbitrarily assessed national income taxes and onerous delivery quotas.
subfiles.title: Report of Agricultural Survey Trip by Jay Dixon Edwards, Second Secretary of Mission, to Four Prefectures in Northern Honshu, Japan, During the Period July 14 to 24, 1948
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.about: Authorizes the U.S. Member of the Far Eastern Commission to oppose British amendments and propose a U.S. amendment regarding gradual implementation of farmers' organization policies.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman (Assistant Secretary of State for Occupied Areas)
subfiles.summary: Authorizes the U.S. Member to oppose British amendments and propose a U.S. amendment providing gradual implementation of farmers' organization policies.

subfiles.from: Joint Chiefs of Staff / State, Army, Navy, Air Force Departments
subfiles.summary: Sets forth policy guiding SCAP to foster democratic, voluntary farmers' cooperatives and unions, protect them from government or commercial domination, and ensure reasonable credit access.
